text:
Chandler Stephenson has two Stanley Cup rings, from Washington in 2018 and Vegas in 2023, and right now he's a passer first, second and third. Ten of his 12 points are assists, and he has put just 11 shots on goal in 15 games. That's a style more than a slump, and it works as long as his wingers finish.

The worry is what happens when the other team has the puck. Seattle gets only 38% of the shot attempts at five on five with Stephenson out there, and its expected-goal share is eight points worse than when he sits. Evolving-Hockey had opponents creating more against him last season than against almost any forward in the league, though its notes also say he played with weaker teammates than nearly anyone, which softens the verdict. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has most of his shots coming off the rush, which fits his legs (81st percentile in top speed). Our projection's middle case is about 12 more goals, so expect the assists to keep doing the talking.
headline: A passer first, second and third
